life_summary: Francis Marion Lyman was born in Illinois in 1840 and participated in the westward Mormon migration with his family, settling in Salt Lake Valley in 1848 at age eight. He helped drive livestock across the plains as part of the pioneer companies. Lyman came of age in the Utah Territory and developed skills in settlement leadership and political engagement. He presided over settlements in Fillmore and Tooele County, and gained recognition for his civic engagement, particularly for fighting government corruption during electoral disputes. His family legacy included both his father Amasa M. Lyman and his son Richard R. Lyman serving as apostles.
church_summary: Lyman was baptized at age eight and served two missions to England, with the first around 1860 and the second in 1873. His second mission expanded throughout Europe, visiting and proselytizing in Wales, Scotland, Denmark, Germany, Switzerland, and France. He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and became president of that quorum in 1903. As an apostle, he conducted missionary work among Native Americans and oversaw the European Mission beginning in 1901. Lyman died of pneumonia in 1916, leaving a legacy of missionary service and ecclesiastical leadership.
